about.eyebrow: Mechanical Engineering — Stevens Institute of Technology
about.bodyP1: I'm a mechanical engineering student at Stevens Institute of Technology, and most of what I know about design I learned by making the part first and drawing it second. I spend my week split between the machine shop and the CAD workstation — running mills and lathes on one side, modeling and tolerancing on the other — which is exactly the loop I want to keep running in aerospace: design something, understand how it's actually manufactured, and make it better because of that.
about.bodyP2: As President of Stevens' SAE BAJA Racing Team, I collaborate with every subteam to design, analyze, and manufacture 400+ parts, and I led the acquisition of a $100,000 fiber laser cutter for student engineering organizations. As Head TA for a manufacturing course, I teach GD&T, CMM, CAM, and DFM to the next group of students coming through the shop I work in.

coursework: Frontiers of Tech: A.I. & Machine Learning

timeline.title: Eagle Hill School, Massachusetts
timeline.text: Where I found my footing in design and building. Squash captain, cross-country manager, film club president, student government, and a curriculum committee member. Hudson Valley roots, with stops in South Carolina and Massachusetts.

timeline.title: Camp Counselor
timeline.text: Supervised dorms, assisted in the classroom, and taught a science class where students built and launched model rockets.

timeline.title: Making things for fun
timeline.text: Scuba certification, a leather-bound book with handmade paper, a laser-cut caffeine molecule, a forged rebar fire stand, and electroplating inspired by rocket-nozzle cooling.

timeline.title: Stevens Institute of Technology
timeline.text: Started my B.E. in Mechanical Engineering. 3.58 GPA, Dean's List three semesters, now a junior.

timeline.title: SAE BAJA: first builds
timeline.text: Designed and welded drivetrain guarding, then led the braking system. Also built an automatic plant waterer and a phone-controlled door opener.

timeline.title: Machine Shop and Metamaterials Research
timeline.text: Joined the machine shop, machining parts for a hypersonic wind tunnel and a wave tank, and researched roton structures in a vibrations lab.

timeline.title: Head Teaching Assistant
timeline.text: Promoted after one semester to lead lectures and labs on GD&T, CAM, metrology, and welding.

timeline.title: President of SAE BAJA
timeline.text: Leading 40+ members and every subteam, and bringing a $100,000 fiber laser cutter to campus for student organizations.

timeline.title: Aerospace internships and beyond
timeline.text: Looking to join a team at the top of its field, pushing the envelope forward.

statements.head: Why aerospace
statements.text: I have always been drawn to aerospace. What pulled me in was small, focused teams building machines that push the limits of what people thought possible. That idea of teamwork, close to the machine floor and moving fast, is why I've given so much time to SAE Baja and why I want to build flight hardware.

statements.head: Always learning
statements.text: By the end of my sophomore year I was chosen president of the most technically challenging club on campus, taught a class covering material outside the curriculum, acquired a $100,000 machine for the school without a formal process existing, and started summer research. I know there is far more to learn, and I do my best work collaborating with others.

statements.head: Leading SAE Baja
statements.text: Three years, three vehicles, each outperforming the last. I designed and built the braking system, served as recording secretary, and was elected president. I now lead 40+ members, coordinate subteams, set timelines, and oversee vehicle design, and I teach a class that takes an idea through the engineering process to a part students machine themselves on CNC equipment.

statements.head: Earning trust
statements.text: I earn trust by staying methodical, dependable, and never demanding of others. In high school that meant captaining squash, managing cross-country, and leading the film club. In college it's the machine shop, teaching, and running Baja. I meet deadlines, exceed expectations, and show up for the people around me.

statements.head: Learning outside the classroom
statements.text: Tools are a means to an end. My real growth has been in design: spotting clearance problems early, using standards whenever possible, defining goals and constraints before the first sketch, and applying DFM, FEA, and CFD from concept through machining, testing, and integration.

bullets: Machine stainless and aluminum parts for high-speed imaging in a hypersonic wind tunnel, and built a wave actuator for a 300 ft wave tank.
Designed, manufactured, and assembled 20+ parts for a biomass 3D printer motion system.
Troubleshot and repaired 30 3D printers, 3 mills, 2 lathes, and 2 welders; ran CMM inspection and sandblasting.
Work with clients to define part requirements and limits on time, cost, and tooling, then make, measure, and invoice. Increased shop throughput and cleared project backlogs.
Consult with students and professors on Design for Manufacturability (DFM). Worked 33 hours a week in summer 2025.
Promoted to Head TA after one semester. Led 10+ machining labs on CNC mills and lathes, GD&T, CMM, metrology, welding, and cold forming.
Expand and update content, style, and flow of 10+ lectures.
Instruct in weekly lectures on manufacturing, measuring, and design theory and techniques.

experience.org: Vibrations of Metamaterials · Stevens Institute of Technology
bullets: Researched metamaterials, dispersion diagrams, evanescent waves, non-reciprocity, and vibrational dynamics in elastic materials.
Co-designed a roton structure to restrict vibrational energy to a narrow frequency band.
Assembled and calibrated a surface-mount machine.
Compiled all research into a poster and presented it to a panel of experts.
Supervised students in dorms and assisted teachers with daily lesson plans.
Taught a hands-on science class where students built and launched model rockets.
Ran activities and kept transitions smooth between free time and academic sessions.

projects.title: SAE BAJA Racing Team
paragraphs: Collaborate with all subteams to design, analyze, and manufacture 400+ parts.
Spearheaded the acquisition of a $100,000 fiber laser cutter: 5 months from initial proposal to machine delivery.
Managed a $30,000 semesterly budget, wrote sponsorship packets, and applied for grants and subsidies.
Present the club's objectives to 100+ students at least twice a semester.

Led the vehicle through three builds in three years; TIG-welded the roll cage so the tube bends before the weld breaks. Fabricated suspension parts and carbon fiber body panels, applying DFM, FEA, and CFD.

projects.title: Brakes & Pedals
paragraphs: Led design, research, manufacturing, and testing of 20+ parts for the braking system and pedals.
Developed calculators for pedal length, line pressure, caliper size, and master cylinder size.
Also served as Secretary of Recording, managing schedules and logistics for 20+ members.

projects.title: Drivetrain Guarding
paragraphs: Researched, designed, manufactured, and welded aluminum drivetrain component guarding.

projects.title: Autonomous Boat Design
paragraphs: Led a student team through planning and rapid prototyping of an autonomous boat. Chose a catamaran hull for stability at slow speeds after testing several designs.
Taught myself CFD to improve hydrodynamics and turning radius, simplified geometry to cut print time and supports, and wrote a full technical report and presentation.

projects.title: Automatic Door Opener
paragraphs: Designed a mechanism that opens a dorm door from a phone app: 3D printed the parts, coded an Arduino with a servo motor, installed it, and debugged hardware and software.
Presented the project to other students, covering the process and inspiration.

projects.title: Automatic Plant Waterer
paragraphs: Led a team of three to build a plant watering system: SolidWorks enclosure, Arduino watering logic, 3D printed housing, calibrated to water at the optimal time.

projects.title: Electroplating
paragraphs: Inspired by electroplated fuel ducts in rocket nozzles, I read research papers and built a scaled-down setup in my garage from everyday materials.
Nickel- and copper-plated coins, a metal mug, and older welded projects, learning to substitute materials and teach myself without a classroom.

projects.title: Handmade Builds
paragraphs: A leather-bound book with recycled-newspaper paper, laser-cut wood covers, embossing, and marbled endpapers. A laser-cut caffeine molecule model.
A forged and welded rebar fire stand, using a custom jig so every bend was repeatable.
